verdicts.title: The 'Maximum Quality' integration profile is a placebo -- it produces byte-identical settings to Balanced
verdicts.reasoning: Read the current source myself. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/imaging/integration_settings.dart:737 is exactly `case IntegrationPreset.maximumQuality:` and returns const IntegrationSettings(resampler: lanczos3, weighting: snrSquared, generateRejectionMap: true, cosmeticCorrection: true, outputBitDepth: f32, sourcePreset: maximumQuality). Every one of those five values is already the constructor default (:670 resampler lanczos3, :674 weighting snrSquared, :688 generateRejectionMap true, :689 cosmeticCorrection true, :690 outputBitDepth f32), and balanced at :733 is `const IntegrationSettings(sourcePreset: balanced)` i.e. all defaults. The two objects therefore differ only in `sourcePreset`, and grepping every consumer of sourcePreset in packages/ and apps/ finds exactly one non-test use -- integration_settings_panel.dart:51 `active: _s.sourcePreset`, which only decides which chip is highlighted. Nothing in toBridgeSettings or the native path reads it. Cited file:line is exact.

verdicts.title: sub_gallery_panel.dart (601 lines) is built by no screen -- only by a widget test -- while the code claims the narrative view uses it
verdicts.reasoning: grep -rn 'SubGalleryPanel' over packages/ and apps/ returns the class definition itself plus three comment mentions in sub_cull_rail.dart and exactly one construction: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/session_review/sub_cull_rail_dynamic_subs_test.dart:102. narrative_view.dart builds NightReportPanel (verdict + findings), ImprovementCurvePanel and GrowthCurvePanel and nothing else -- no sub grid, no gallery. The false claim is verbatim at sub_cull_rail.dart:24: 'One controller, two renderings: the narrative screen uses [SubGalleryPanel]'. Location correct; P3 is right (dead 601-line widget plus a comment that lies about the shipped composition).

verdicts.title: The stack result's 'Avg HFR' statistic never renders because the service hard-codes avgHfr: null, even though every selected sub carries an HFR
verdicts.reasoning: Both cited lines are exact in the current tree. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_and_share_service.dart:425 is `avgHfr: null,` (unconditional, in the single StackAndShareResult construction the run persists), and packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/stack_result/stack_result_screen.dart:522 is `if (result.avgHfr != null)` guarding the 'Avg HFR' _StatRow. No other local producer sets it -- the only other assignment is stacking_operations.dart:251 reading avgHfr back off a remote host's JSON, which is fed by this same null on the host, and stacked_results_dao.dart:164 reading the column back. So on the local path the column is always NULL and the row can never render. Note the source now carries a justification comment ('the live-stacking engine does not measure HFR ... a later analysis pass may populate it'), so this is a known gap rather than an oversight, but the finding's factual claim -- dead UI row, hard-coded null -- holds and the file:line is right. P3 is correct.

verdicts.title: The standalone /science route can never build ScienceScreen -- its redirect always fires, so the screen class and its Scaffold are unreachable code
verdicts.reasoning: packages/skotiq_app/lib/router/app_router.dart:222-236 is exactly as described: the GoRoute for '/science' declares `redirect: (context, state) { final sub = state.uri.queryParameters['tab']; return '/analytics?tab=science...'; }` -- an unconditional non-null return -- and then a pageBuilder constructing ScienceScreen. go_router short-circuits a route whose redirect returns non-null, so the pageBuilder is unreachable. app_router.dart:232 is the only construction of ScienceScreen anywhere in packages/ or apps/ (the only other hits are the class definition at science_screen.dart:246/249 and a doc comment at :42). Cited locations exact. Severity P3 is generous -- the only cost is dead code plus the trap it sets for the next editor -- but not wrong.

verdicts.title: The Share Card's metadata strip is clipped: it renders 'M51  Integration 00:35:00  Frames 7  Fil…' and the filter is cut off the right edge
verdicts.reasoning: Recomputed the geometry myself rather than trusting the screenshot. I ran the shipped ShareCardRenderer against the exact spec stack_result_screen.dart:852 builds (title 'M51', stats Integration 00:35:00 / Frames 7 / Filter L, targetWidth=targetHeight=result dimensions=512). fontForHeight(512) -> 512*0.04 = 20.5 -> img.arial24, lineHeight 28, pad 14, gap 11. Summing xAdvance exactly as _drawBottomBar does: 'M51' 14..60, 'Integration  00:35:00' 93..311, 'Frames  7' 344..452, 'Filter  L' starts at 485 and needs 80px -> ends at 565, i.e. 53px past the 512px right edge. Rendering the PNG for real and scanning the caption band confirms bright glyph pixels run all the way to column 511, so the last segment is cut mid-word exactly as reported. Nothing in the renderer measures the caption against the card WIDTH: the only width logic is the `if (x >= bitmap.width - pad) break;` bail-out, and drawString clips the rest. Location partly wrong: ShareCardSpec is at stack_and_share_models.dart:642-676 (fontScale default scaleToHeight, layout bottomBar) as claimed, but the composition that actually truncates is share_card_renderer.dart:360-447 _drawBottomBar, NOT stack_share_export_service.dart -- that service only forwards to _cardRenderer at :344.
verdicts.location_wrong: Truncating code is packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/share_card_renderer.dart:360-447 (_drawBottomBar), not stack_share_export_service.dart; the spec itself is stack_and_share_models.dart:642-676 as cited.

verdicts.title: In the Submit-discovery dialog all three network chips are dead on a default install, and only the currently-selected network's blocker is explained
verdicts.reasoning: Verified in the current source at the cited lines. transient_report_panel.dart:127-140 renders the three TransientReportFormat chips with `onTap: enabled ? () => setState(...) : null` where enabled = _formatEnabled(...), and :142-151 renders _disabledReason ONLY for `_format` (the selected one) -- the other two networks' blockers are never shown. _formatEnabled at :343-367 gates every format on `d.reviewed` first, then aavso on aavsoAvailable + a non-empty settings.aavsoObserverCode, mpc on a non-empty mpcObservatoryCode + a plausible-mover kind, tns on complete bot creds, so on a default install with empty ScienceSettings all three are false. I also checked the widget the chip is: skotiq_chip.dart:65-68 returns the bare chip when onTap is null -- same fill, same border, same text colour as an enabled unselected chip, no Semantics, no cursor change -- so a disabled chip is visually indistinguishable from a live one and silently swallows the tap, exactly as reported. Preview/Copy at :296-320 are gated the same way. Cited file:lines are exact. ALSO REPRODUCED LIVE on the rebuilt bundle (profile v2-science-review, display :86): I seeded one newSource detection, confirmed it (DB reviewed=1), opened First Light > Submit. The dialog opens on TNS with the amber 'TNS submission needs your bot id/name, reporting group, data source, reporter, and api key' line; clicking the AAVSO chip changes nothing -- TNS stays selected and the TNS-specific reason stays on screen (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-12.png before, v2sr-13.png after). AAVSO and MPC render with the same fill/border/text colour as a live chip.

verdicts.title: Confirming a First Light candidate does not update the Observing Alerts tab beside it: the same detection reads 'Confirmed' on one sub-tab and 'New' on the next
verdicts.reasoning: The symptom is real, but the finding's cause and its 'where' are wrong, and that matters because the cited file is not the one to fix. transient_alert_mapper.dart:66-70 does map reviewed -> TransientAlertState.acknowledged, and the alert list IS rebuilt: activeTransientAlertsProvider is a StreamProvider.autoDispose that holds `ref.listen(allTransientDetectionsProvider, ...)` (transient_alert_provider.dart:552-556) and re-merges on every change, with allTransientDetectionsProvider itself a drift watchRecentDetections live query (transient_detections_provider.dart:95-100) that re-emits when the local markReviewed writes the row. The real reason the badge stays 'New' is that the Observing Alerts UI never reads the alert's own state: transients_screen.dart:122 watches transientAlertStatesProvider, :143 does `final alertState = states[alert.id]`, and transient_card.dart:56 falls back to `TransientAlertState.newAlert` when that map has no entry; _filterAlerts (:167-172) puts exactly those under the 'New' filter. transientAlertStatesProvider is only ever populated from the persisted `transient_alert_state_<id>` settings rows written by the user's own queue/dismiss/acknowledge actions (transient_alert_provider.dart:683-810) -- nothing seeds it from TransientAlert.state, so the mapper's `acknowledged` is dead on this surface for every First Light row. So: CONFIRMED as a defect, wrong location. REPRODUCED LIVE on the rebuilt bundle: seeded detection id 1 (newSource, reviewed=0), Analytics > Science > First Light > Confirm -> DB reviewed=1 and the card badge reads 'Confirmed' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-12.png shows the 'Confirmed' badge behind the dialog); one tab across, Observing Alerts shows the same detection as 'NS J13.50+47.2 ... Supernova' with a blue 'New' badge (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-11.png). So the disagreement survives the fix wave.
verdicts.location_wrong: Cause is packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/transients/transients_screen.dart:122/143/167-172 + widgets/transient_card.dart:56 (card state comes from transientAlertStatesProvider, TransientAlert.state is ignored), NOT 'transient_alert_provider.dart -- the alert list is not invalidated'; the list IS re-merged via ref.listen at transient_alert_provider.dart:552-556.

verdicts.title: Science CSV exports never ask where to save and write to a hard-coded ~/Documents/Skotiq/exports, ignoring the app's configured data directory
verdicts.reasoning: science_export_hub.dart:41-48 defines scienceExportDirectoryProvider as getApplicationDocumentsDirectory() + 'Skotiq/exports', created on demand; _exportData at :726-855 builds the CSV, reads that provider at :826, joins a timestamped filename and writes it with no picker anywhere in the path -- the only user-facing surface is the `Exported N rows to <path>` string at :831. getApplicationDocumentsDirectory is path_provider's XDG documents dir, which nothing in the app's SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR / SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR plumbing overrides, so the claim that the export ignores the configured data directory holds. The contrast the finding draws is also real: the stack-result exports go through stackResultSavePickerProvider with a dialogTitle/fileName (stack_result_screen.dart:869-874). Location correct. Severity: I would call this P3 rather than P2 -- the file is written, the full path is reported in the result line, and on mobile revealExportedFile(:846) hands it to the share sheet; the harm is an unexpected location and a shared collision point, not lost data.

verdicts.title: The cull rail advertises 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' from a curve it already knows is stale; pressing it always refuses, and its advice ('re-integrate to refresh') reproduces the same stale curve
verdicts.reasoning: The render-time/press-time asymmetry the finding describes is exactly what the current source does, and the two cited widget lines are exact. sub_cull_rail.dart:274 passes the action through whenever `curve != null && curve.recommendation.keepN > 0` -- no population check, no gain check -- and :470-480 then renders an enabled primary SkotiqButton labelled 'Keep best $keepN (+${gainPct.toStringAsFixed(0)}%)' (:475) inside a Tooltip 'Drop to the optimizer-recommended best $keepN subs (+…% SNR)' (:473). Every staleness test lives in the press handler instead: SessionReviewController.cullToRecommended() bails with CullToRecommendedResult.staleCurve when the curve's population length differs from the accepted set, when paths duplicate, or when any population path is no longer accepted, and with alreadyOptimal when keepN >= population.length. So the control can only ever be pressed to be refused in those states, while still advertising a specific quantified action. Note this is NOT contingent on the P0 that produced the 1-frame master: any accept/reject after an integration diverges the population, and the alreadyOptimal case renders a '+0%' button that also refuses. Location: the sub_cull_rail.dart:473/475 citations are exact; the controller guard is now at session_review_controller.dart:1418 (the finding said :1354 -- the file grew 66 lines in the P0/P1 fix wave), so use the function name, not that number.
verdicts.location_wrong: cullToRecommended() is at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/session_review_controller.dart:1418-1480 in the rebuilt tree, not :1354; sub_cull_rail.dart:473/475 are exact.

verdicts.title: Running an A/B recipe preview leaves a full 'Preview... 100%' progress bar pinned under the header forever, so the screen permanently claims a job is running
verdicts.reasoning: Traced the whole loop in the current source. native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/post_session.rs:838 ends the preview integrate with `emit_integration_progress("preview", FRACTION_DONE, None, None)` -- a terminal 1.0 on the shared integrationProgress stream. session_review_controller.dart:561-577 _bindProgress() writes every event straight onto state.progress and deliberately leaves a terminal fraction on screen ('left on screen until the action's own completion handler clears it'). session_review_screen.dart:142-144 renders _ProgressStrip for as long as `progress != null`, labelling the raw phase token as 'Preview…' (_phaseLabel at :282). The only code that ever clears it is integrate() (clearProgress + clearLiveProgress at :796-797 and :808-809) and the stream's onError (:573). reIntegratePreview() at :1022-1042 -- the method the A/B panel's 'Run both' calls -- returns its outcome with no clear on any path, so the 100% strip is orphaned exactly as reported. Location: the file/function citations are right but both line numbers drifted in the fix wave (_bindProgress is :561 not :515, reIntegratePreview :1022 not :976, _ProgressStrip :142 not :119). I did not re-drive this live: reproducing it needs a session with real FITS subs on disk, which the scratch profile has none of; the mechanism above is complete and unambiguous.
verdicts.location_wrong: Current lines: _bindProgress session_review_controller.dart:561, reIntegratePreview :1022, strip session_review_screen.dart:142-144 (finding cited :515/:976/:119).

verdicts.title: A/B recipe compare declared 'tie 1 vs 1' when both recipes had silently dropped 8 of 9 subs
verdicts.reasoning: The word doing the work in this finding is 'silently', and the panel is in fact the one surface in the whole flow that does report the drop -- twice per recipe. ab_compare_panel.dart:284 renders MasterPreviewView.fromOutcome, whose stat line (master_preview_view.dart:33-42) is '${framesIntegrated} frames · ${framesRejected} rejected · <time> · residual <x> px', and :287-289 renders a _StatBlock (:459-497) whose first two chips are literally 'Integrated 1' and 'Rejected 8'. So a run that kept 1 of 9 shows '1 frames · 8 rejected' and 'Rejected 8' on BOTH recipe cards, directly above the verdict row. The verdict row itself is also not a false statement: _cmp (:591-595) compares framesIntegrated and returns '=' when they are equal, which is rendered as 'tie' (:642) beside the true detail '1 vs 1' -- the two recipes did keep the same number of frames. What is left of the finding is a request for an extra 'neither result is comparable' callout when framesIntegrated is far below the accepted count. That is a reasonable enhancement (P4 at most), not a defect, and the premise it was filed on -- that the panel hid the drop -- is contradicted by the panel's own code. ab_compare_panel.dart is unmodified since the finding was written, so this is not a 'fixed since' case; it was wrong when filed.

verdicts.title: Stack & Share surfaces the raw Rust error enum to the user: 'SkotiqError.imageError(field0: ...)'
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by following the string end to end. The bridge error is a freezed union: packages/skotiq_bridge/lib/src/error.dart:85 `const factory SkotiqError.imageError(String field0)`, and the generated toString is verbatim `return 'SkotiqError.imageError(field0: $field0)';` at error.freezed.dart:1557 -- so the FRB positional-field label really is in the string. stack_and_share_provider.dart:234 catches whatever the run threw and stores `errorMessage: e.toString()` unmodified; stack_and_share_dialog.dart:243-245 hands that to _buildError, which at :258-282 special-cases only the live-stacking-busy case and otherwise renders the raw string as the message of a 'Stack & Share failed' SkotiqAlert. There is no mapping table, no technical-details disclosure, and no other error path that would sanitise it (the only pre-formatted message is the remote-backend refusal at :171-176). Location fine -- though the toString actually happens at stack_and_share_provider.dart:234, so a fixer should start there, not in the dialog. Severity: this is presentation polish on an already-legible sentence, so P3 rather than P2.
verdicts.location_wrong: The raw stringification is packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/stack_and_share_provider.dart:234 (`errorMessage: e.toString()`); the dialog at stack_and_share_dialog.dart:258-282 only renders it.

verdicts.title: After session recovery the imaging Session card says 'Captured 0 frames' while the line under it says 'Integration 40m 0s'
verdicts.reasoning: REPRODUCED LIVE on the rebuilt bundle. I seeded imaging_sessions id 1 with status='active', end_time=null, successful_exposures=8, total_integration_secs=2400 in the scratch DB (/tmp/ns-audit/v2-science-review/data/skotiq.db), restarted, took 'Incomplete Sessions Found' > Resume (the dialog itself correctly read '8 exposures / 40m total', /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-03.png), then opened Imaging: the Session card reads 'Captured 0 frames' immediately above 'Integration 40m 0s' and 'Status Active' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-05.png). Cause is exactly as cited: capture_panel.dart:75 takes the count from recentSessionFramesProvider, which on a non-network backend is just sessionImagesProvider (imaging_provider.dart:377) -- a StateNotifier<List<CapturedImage>> seeded with `[]` every app launch (:328-330) -- and renders it at :206-208, while :221-231 renders sessionState.totalIntegrationSecs, which SessionService.recoverSession restores from the DB row along with completedExposures = session.successfulExposures (session_service.dart:505-512). So the restored exposure count exists in state and the card ignores it. Cited file:lines are accurate.
